summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on an unexpected drop in KV/prefix cache hit rate for longer prompt flows. Reviewed recent metrics, root-cause hypotheses (eviction TTLs, prompt canonicalization, batch amplification), agreed on three short experiments and next steps for runbook + A/B.
transcript:
Header: 2026-11-30 16:00 UTC | Duration: 38m | Attendees: Maya Chen, Evan Park (Redwood); Jasmine Kumar, Diego Alvarez, Lena Brooks, Omar Farouk (Sparrow)

Auto-summary (brief): noted a regression in cache hit rate for long conversational prompts after last week's prefetch patch; discussed mitigation experiments and who will own them.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick check—can you see my screen?
00:06 Speaker 2 (Jasmine): yep all good here
00:09 Speaker 1 (Maya): cool ok we'll keep to ~35 minutes, main thing today is the KV/prefix hit-rate anomaly that popped up after the prefetch changes we pushed last week. Evan and I will walk through the metrics and then we want to propose three short experiments.
00:26 Speaker 3 (Evan): quick note, data's in the dashboard link we shared earlier — i pulled raw CSVs too just in case the charts hide something.
00:35 Speaker 4 (Diego): thanks, we saw a drop in end-to-end success rates on the long-flow cohort, so keen to understand.
00:42 Speaker 2 (Jasmine): yeah we had a bunch of sandbox jobs show lower reuse for prompts longer than ~512 tokens, hit-rate fell from ~48% to ~22% for those sessions. shorter prompts still looked ok.
00:57 Speaker 3 (Evan): right and to be precise, aggregate KV hit rate across all traffic went from 41% -> 36% which is fine, but the long-prompt cohort — which is about 9% of traffic — dropped sharply and that's what skewed user-visible perf.
01:10 Speaker 5 (Lena): is this definitely tied to the prefetch patch, or could there be an indexing problem?
01:16 Speaker 3 (Evan): good question, we traced request ids and sequence lengths — the prefetch change increased aggressive prefetch for sessions we thought were similar, but for long prompts we may have created many small, non-canonical keys. basically canonicalization mismatch and TTL.
01:34 Speaker 2 (Jasmine): when you say non-canonical keys you mean the prefix hashing changed? we still use normalized prefix plus session id right?
01:41 Speaker 3 (Evan): we used the same prefix algorithm but prefetch created partial-prefix entries with truncated tokens — so hit rate for full-prefix lookups dropped. also TTL eviction was shorter for prefetched entries which didn't survive the inter-request gap.
01:58 Speaker 1 (Maya): ok so hypothesis A: prefetch created short-lived fragments; hypothesis B: prompt normalization needs to be applied before keying; hypothesis C: batching interaction increased latency causing windows to miss.
02:14 Speaker 4 (Diego): latency windows? elaborate.
02:17 Speaker 3 (Evan): when we batch larger at tail requests, p95 jumped from ~180ms to ~240ms on those long flows — so inter-arrival assumptions for cache reuse broke; some sessions waited longer and the prefetched fragments expired.
02:34 Speaker 6 (Omar): that's rough, our SLO is p95 <200ms so that spike is visible.
02:38 Speaker 1 (Maya): agreed, we want to avoid hitting your SLO. the quick fixes we propose are: 1) increase TTL for prefetched fragments for long-flow cohorts, 2) add prompt canonicalization pass before keying, 3) switch to fixed prefix grouping for the affected cohort to reduce fragment proliferation.
02:56 Speaker 2 (Jasmine): can we do a canary for just 5% of long flows?
03:00 Speaker 3 (Evan): yes we'll do a canary. rough plan: Redwood will push three small changes behind feature flags and run each at 5% then 20% if positive. we'll capture raw hit-rate, p95, cost delta.
03:16 Speaker 5 (Lena): what about eviction policy — do you have an auto-extension option when we see activity?
03:22 Speaker 3 (Evan): not currently automatic; we can do TTL tiers based on session length heuristics. that's on our short list for the experiment.
03:31 Speaker 2 (Jasmine): any immediate rollback if canary looks bad?
03:34 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes canary will be toggleable, we also will have fallbacks to a smaller model variant if latency rises beyond your threshold.
03:43 Speaker 4 (Diego): security question — if we change keying, could that impact PII handling or KMS logs?
03:49 Speaker 1 (Maya): good point. canonicalization will be done client-side by you or within Redwood before keying — in either case we can ensure we never persist raw PII in keys; we use HMAC with KMS for key derivation on the private deployment.
04:05 Speaker 6 (Omar): we need the KMS rotation policy confirmed; we have a compliance window next month.
04:10 Speaker 1 (Maya): noted, Diego/Omar we'll add that to action items. Evan, can you talk through the dashboard numbers?
04:16 Speaker 3 (Evan): sure pulling up the chart — ok so panel A shows prefix hit-rate by length bucket. last Monday we rolled prefetch v2. for <256 token prompts hit-rate actually rose from 60% to 68%, which matches expectations. for 256-1024 tokens we saw 48% -> 22% on Wednesday after traffic churn. cost for prefetch rose ~3% on aggregate.
04:44 Speaker 2 (Jasmine): is the 22% stable? it's not ephemeral?
04:47 Speaker 3 (Evan): it persisted for ~36 hours, then we applied a small TTL bump in a dev run which brought it to ~31% but still below baseline. the dev patch wasn't in prod so it's noisy.
05:01 Speaker 5 (Lena): any evidence of cache key collisions?
05:04 Speaker 3 (Evan): collisions low, the issue is more fragmentation — many distinct keys for what is conceptually the same prefix, due to white-space/stopword differences and prompt-metadata tokens.
05:18 Speaker 2 (Jasmine): ok so prompt normalization could help a lot. we have internal linting that strips timestamps and request-ids, but we don't canonicalize expansions. we can add that quickly.
05:29 Speaker 3 (Evan): great, that would reduce key cardinality. Redwood can add a normalization shim in-flight too but customer-side is preferable for PII reasons.
05:40 Speaker 4 (Diego): what's the expected impact if we canonicalize? ballpark numbers?
05:44 Speaker 3 (Evan): conservative estimate — reduce unique key count by ~35% in the affected bucket, which should push hit-rate from 22% up to mid-40s if TTL remains the same. with TTL bump we can aim for 55-60%.
05:58 Speaker 1 (Maya): ok target for the pilot: hit-rate >50% for the long-prompt cohort and p95 <200ms. we should track cost delta — we don't want to double cost.
06:09 Speaker 2 (Jasmine): do we have a cost estimate for increased TTL?
06:12 Speaker 3 (Evan): rough: every 10% increase in TTL for the cohort gives ~2.5% unit token cost increase; exact depends on reuse curve. I'll share a more precise calc.
06:23 Speaker 5 (Lena): can we tighten batching? batching improvements earlier may have amplified the latency.
06:27 Speaker 3 (Evan): yes we can bound batch sizes for the long cohort to keep p95 down; Redwood runtime has a per-route batch cap we can adjust.
06:36 Speaker 2 (Jasmine): we also noticed some prompt-eviction patterns when the platform scaled down idle GPUs — could that be the cause too?
06:43 Speaker 3 (Evan): that can contribute — when dedicated pool scales down, KV warm entries can be lost if the node restarts and cache is local. for your pilot we are using a shared redis-backed cluster but we saw node churn in the private sim which impacted warm state.
06:59 Speaker 6 (Omar): if state is lost on scale events, can we snapshot session state?
07:02 Speaker 3 (Evan): we have session snapshotting but not for the small fragments; we can enable persistent snapshots for the cohort as part of experiment 2.
07:12 Speaker 1 (Maya): let's go through the three experiments and owners quickly.
07:15 Speaker 3 (Evan): Experiment 1 (E1): Prompt canonicalization at the customer side + Redwood verification; Canaries at 5/20/100% — measure hit-rate delta and p95. Owner: Jasmine + Redwood SE (Evan).
07:28 Speaker 1 (Maya): Experiment 2 (E2): Increase TTL for prefetched fragments for sessions >512 tokens + enable session snapshot for that cohort. Owner: Redwood infra (Evan) + Customer (Diego) to validate persistence.
07:44 Speaker 3 (Evan): Experiment 3 (E3): Fixed prefix grouping for the cohort to reduce cardinality + per-route batch cap to bound latency. Owner: Redwood runtime (Evan).
07:58 Speaker 2 (Jasmine): timeline? we want quick wins in first week.
08:01 Speaker 3 (Evan): propose 48-72h canaries per experiment; start E1 this Friday 2026-12-04, E2 after initial E1 signals (can overlap small percentages), E3 last if needed.
08:14 Speaker 5 (Lena): who logs the raw data and where? we need S3 exports for audit.
08:18 Speaker 3 (Evan): Redwood will export raw CSVs to an S3 bucket you control using the same role you provided — Jasmine pls confirm bucket and prefix.
08:28 Speaker 2 (Jasmine): will confirm by tomorrow.
08:30 Speaker 6 (Omar): on security, confirm that keys are derived and we don't store PII in cache keys.
08:35 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes we use HMAC plus salt; for private deployment we can use your KMS for derivation. I'll attach the KMS flow doc.
08:42 Speaker 4 (Diego): one more ask — can Redwood run a dedicated perf run that mimics our 90th percentile long prompt mix? we want to see p95 under load.
08:50 Speaker 3 (Evan): yes we can. Redwood will spin a dedicated pool (short-lived) with the same traffic generator, run the baseline and patched configs and share the p50/p95/p99.
09:03 Speaker 1 (Maya): ok let's capture action items — Evan will push the prefix grouping patch and TTL knobs, Jasmine will send canonicalization snippet and S3 details, Maya will send pilot extension and pricing.
09:18 Speaker 2 (Jasmine): quick question — you mentioned fallback to smaller model variant. how transparent is that?
09:22 Speaker 3 (Evan): it's a policy switch in the smart router — we can route to a cheaper compatible variant on high latency, results are slightly lower quality but keep SLA. it's instantaneous to flip.
09:34 Speaker 5 (Lena): ok that's useful for burst protection.
09:38 Speaker 1 (Maya): any final questions?
09:41 Speaker 2 (Jasmine): none from me, thanks.
09:42 Speaker 4 (Diego): none, thanks team.
09:43 Speaker 1 (Maya): we'll share notes and runbook by end-of-day tomorrow and target experiments starting Friday. thanks everyone.
09:50 End of recording.
